title: Bismuth main agent turn output
description: The complete output of one main agent turn. The runtime performs the intents in listed order, writing a trace event for each. An empty list means silence.

type.description: Which intent this is. Each type has its own required fields, listed in the main agent prompt.

destination.description: route: memory path the note lands in, relative to the memory root. Must appear in the turn's DESTINATIONS block, or be under others/.

mode.description: route: declared = she named the destination; inferred = the agent chose it; unroutable = parked in others/.

reason.description: route: one line, why this destination. The permanent record of why the note landed where it did.

instruction.description: route/spawn: the complete self-contained instruction for a worker. Absolute paths, exact text, exact operation. Written verbatim to the trace.

kind.description: spawn/route: what the worker is for. search = read-only retrieval; the worker must change nothing and returns its findings in `output`.

claude_md.description: spawn/route: absolute path to a CLAUDE.md the worker should read first, if the target folder has one.

budget_usd.description: spawn/route: optional per-worker spend cap. Omit for the default. schedule_create/schedule_update: the cap for the worker this schedule spawns each time it fires.

name.description: schedule_create/schedule_update: the schedule's handle, e.g. "twitter-daily". Becomes the filename in _schedules/. Lowercase words joined by hyphens.

every.description: schedule_create/schedule_update: "daily", "weekly", or an interval like "3_days". There is no cron syntax and none is wanted.

at.description: schedule_create/schedule_update: wall-clock time, "HH:MM", 24-hour, local. It fires at the next free slot after this time — never earlier, and later if she is mid-conversation or the laptop was shut.

days.description: schedule_create/schedule_update: which weekdays, for every: weekly. Ignored otherwise.

enabled.description: schedule_create/schedule_update: false pauses it. This is how a schedule is stopped — nothing is deleted, so she can un-pause it later.

body.description: schedule_create: the standing instruction, written to the schedule file. A worker reads THIS FILE every time it fires, so write it as a contract for a stranger with four tools, not as a note to yourself. It may use {date} and {MEMORY}; the SYSTEM block gives you both when it fires. On schedule_update, omit it to keep the existing body unchanged.

produces.description: schedule_create/schedule_update: the artifact this schedule must leave behind, relative to the memory root, e.g. "projects/x/daily/{date}.txt". The runtime checks it exists two hours after firing and raises a SYSTEM turn if it does not. Set it whenever the schedule's whole point is a file.

min_bytes.description: schedule_create/schedule_update: smallest believable size for `produces`. A file that exists but is 12 bytes is a failure too.

summary.description: schedule_create/schedule_update: one line, what this schedule is for. It is all you get in the SYSTEM block when it fires, so make it enough to decide on.

task_ref.description: An existing task_id from the TASKS block, or any short label invented for a task created in this same turn; the runtime maps labels to ids.

request.description: task_create: one line describing what she asked for.

state.description: task_create: unclear if the work cannot be fully specified yet, working if it can. `done` is an event, never a state.

question.description: task_ask: the question to send her. One question, her language, smallest thing that unblocks the work.

answer.description: task_clarify: her answer folded into the task, in a form the next instruction can be written from.

text.description: reply/task_done: the message to send her, in Bismuth's own voice. Never a worker's words verbatim.

channel.description: reply: text, or a TTS voice note.
